subproblem.title: Poincaré inequality on the unit cube for functions of variation at most V
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ Euclid n (Lebesgue measure), div g := trace Dg. If u : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integrable on Q₁ and V ∈ ℝ satisfies ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1, then there is c ∈ ℝ with ∫_{Q₁} |u − c| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V = 2^{m+2}√(m + 1) V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (V : ℝ), IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, u y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) ≤ V) → ∃ c : ℝ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - c| ≤ 2 ^ (m + 2) * Real.sqrt (m + 1) * V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median: Poincaré inequality ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV via the limits σ ↓ 0, δ ↓ 0). Departure (a simplification): the limits are run on the double integral of step 2 instead of on the means over Q_δ, so no convergence of means is needed; the final c is the mean u_{Q₁} = ∫_{Q₁}u, as in the parent proof. In Simon this is the BV Poincaré inequality Ch. 2, 2.7 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 627–661) as used for the first line of display (32) in the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1883–1892).

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate and e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ G x, viewed as a linear map). For v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x, which equals the Euclidean length |∇v(x)| of the gradient. Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted Lebesgue measure. Under the measure-preserving, coordinate-preserving continuous linear equivalence WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp / EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp; it is not an isometry for the sup norm of Fin n → ℝ, and no isometry property is used) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ); hence vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded, and Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁ for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Sibling results used. smooth_approx (dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_smooth_approx): for u integrable on Q₁ with hyp(u, V) and δ > 0 there are C¹ functions v_k with ∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ V for all k and ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0. smooth_poincare (dimred_mbl_dt_cbm_smooth_poincare): for C¹ v and δ ≥ 0, ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|v(x) − v(y)| dy dx ≤ K₀∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv‖ with K₀ := 2ⁿ√n = 2^{m+1}√(m + 1).

Fix u integrable on Q₁ and V with hyp(u, V).

0. V ≥ 0: apply hyp to g ≡ 0 (C^∞, compact support, tsupport ∅ ⊆ Q₁, |0| ≤ 1; D0 = 0, trace 0 = 0): 0 = ∫_{Q₁} u · 0 ≤ V.

1. Finiteness. Since u is integrable on Q₁ and vol(Q₁) = 1 < ∞, the function (x, y) ↦ |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ |u(x)| + |u(y)| is integrable on Q₁ × Q₁ (product of the restricted measures; it is a.e.-strongly measurable as a composition of the a.e.-strongly measurable functions (x, y) ↦ u(x) and (x, y) ↦ u(y)). For every x and every δ ≥ 0 the function y ↦ |u(x) − u(y)| is integrable on Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ (u is integrable there and constants are integrable on sets of finite measure), so h_δ(x) := ∫_{Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| dy is finite, 0 ≤ h_δ(x) ≤ |u(x)| + ∫_{Q₁}|u|, and by Fubini x ↦ h_δ(x) is a.e.-strongly measurable on Q₁; hence h_δ is integrable on Q₁. Put D(δ) := ∫_{Q_δ} h_δ(x) dx = ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| dy dx.

2. D(δ) ≤ K₀V for every δ ∈ (0, 1/2). Fix such δ and take v_k from smooth_approx (δ > 0). Each v_k is continuous, hence bounded on the bounded set Q_δ, say |v_k| ≤ B_k there; so v_k − u is integrable on Q_δ and ε_k := ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u| → 0. The function (x, y) ↦ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| is continuous, hence measurable, and bounded by 2B_k on Q_δ × Q_δ; so d_k(x) := ∫_{Q_δ}|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy satisfies 0 ≤ d_k ≤ 2B_k vol(Q_δ) and is a.e.-strongly measurable (Fubini, Mathlib MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right'), hence integrable on Q_δ. By smooth_poincare (δ ≥ 0), D_k := ∫_{Q_δ} d_k = ∫_{x∈Q_δ}∫_{y∈Q_δ}|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy dx ≤ K₀∫_{Q_δ}‖Dv_k‖ ≤ K₀V. For all x, y: |u(x) − u(y)| ≤ |v_k(x) − v_k(y)| + |u(x) − v_k(x)| + |v_k(y) − u(y)|. For fixed x, integrating in y over Q_δ (all three terms are integrable in y) gives h_δ(x) ≤ d_k(x) + vol(Q_δ)|u(x) − v_k(x)| + ε_k. The three functions of x on the right are integrable on Q_δ (d_k as just shown, |u − v_k| because v_k − u is integrable on Q_δ, and the constant ε_k because vol(Q_δ) < ∞), and h_δ is integrable on Q_δ by step 1; integrating in x over Q_δ and using vol(Q_δ) ≤ 1: D(δ) ≤ D_k + vol(Q_δ)ε_k + vol(Q_δ)ε_k ≤ K₀V + 2ε_k. Letting k → ∞ gives D(δ) ≤ K₀V.

3. D(0) ≤ K₀V. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 3) for j ∈ ℕ; then δ_j ∈ (0, 1/2), δ_j ↓ 0, and every x ∈ Q₁ lies in Q_{δ_j} for all large j. For x ∈ Q₁, 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(y)|u(x) − u(y)| → 1_{Q₁}(y)|u(x) − u(y)| for every y ∈ Q₁, dominated by |u(x) − u(y)|, which is integrable in y over Q₁ for every x (step 1); so by dominated convergence h_{δ_j}(x) → h_0(x) for every x ∈ Q₁. Moreover 0 ≤ 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(x)h_{δ_j}(x) ≤ h_0(x) with h_0 integrable on Q₁, and 1_{Q_{δ_j}}(x)h_{δ_j}(x) → h_0(x) for every x ∈ Q₁. By dominated convergence D(δ_j) = ∫_{Q₁}1_{Q_{δ_j}}h_{δ_j} → ∫_{Q₁}h_0 = D(0). Since D(δ_j) ≤ K₀V for all j by step 2, D(0) ≤ K₀V.

4. Choice of c. Let c := ∫_{Q₁}u. Since vol(Q₁) = 1, for every x: u(x) − c = ∫_{Q₁}(u(x) − u(y)) dy, hence |u(x) − c| ≤ ∫_{Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| dy = h_0(x). Integrating over Q₁ (both sides integrable): ∫_{Q₁}|u − c| ≤ D(0) ≤ K₀V = 2ⁿ√nV ≤ 2^{n+1}√nV, the last step because V ≥ 0 (step 0). With n = m + 1, 2^{n+1}√n = 2^{m+2}√(m + 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: V ≥ 0 from g ≡ 0; |u(x) − u(y)| is integrable on Q₁ × Q₁, so D(δ) := ∫_{Q_δ}∫_{Q_δ}|u(x) − u(y)| is finite.
For δ ∈ (0, 1/2): smooth_approx gives v_k, smooth_poincare gives D_k ≤ 2ⁿ√nV, and D(δ) ≤ D_k + 2∫_{Q_δ}|v_k − u|; letting k → ∞, D(δ) ≤ 2ⁿ√nV.
δ_j = 1/(j + 3) ↓ 0 and dominated convergence give D(0) = ∫_{Q₁}∫_{Q₁}|u(x) − u(y)| ≤ 2ⁿ√nV.

audit.reason: Uses precisely smooth_approx and smooth_poincare. Product integrability justifies the L¹ error comparison, and the two dominated-convergence passages establish the full-cube bound. Choosing the unit-volume mean and using V≥0 gives the exact claimed constant.
